summary: ChatQuestionnaire: the agent asking, inside the thread — a question followed by tappable options, as text rows or as image tiles. Single-select COMMITS on tap, which is why it has no Confirm; multi-select toggles and confirms with the count in the label (the component does not compose that string — pluralisation is language, and every user-visible string is a prop). Answering collapses it to a receipt: the question stays, the answer becomes a selected Badge, the options leave. Its own item rather than a ChatWidget payload: it has NO container, no fill and no action bar, so six of that component's parts mean nothing here — the Text widget sheet asks for three families in one item and the Questionnaire sheet calls itself one of two, and the drawings settle it. SELECTION IS AN EDGE, NEVER A FILL. Card Sorting's active card verbatim: the fill does not move, a 1.5px border-focus edge and a check in the same blue carry the state, and the filled accent stays reserved for Send, Confirm and the answered Badge. That is also what keeps this component clear of the library-wide bg-hover / bg-selected collision — hover is a fill and selection is an edge, so they are on different channels by construction rather than by hoping about order, and the browser test asserts exactly that (a chosen option's fill EQUALS its neighbour's; its edge does not). The options are buttons in a named role="group", not a radiogroup: a press answers the question rather than moving a selection around, so arrow-key roving would be a promise the widget does not keep — recorded, with the condition under which it should change. A handoff option ("Other — tell me in your own words…") submits its own id and selects nothing, because moving the cursor to the composer is the caller's. check:controls gained an eighth exemption with the reason both bespoke controls exist. The sheet's --ui-canvas-selection is a Paper-only token that resolves to --ui-border-focus, which is what ships — and is what makes the two pickers one selection language.
